samples.summary: The PR bundles four independent concerns into one change: (a) OAuth loopback-callback nonce binding (backend controller/store/guard + CLI login + docs), (b) a new URL path-segment encoding/rejection module (`packages/cli/src/client/url.ts`) applied across ~20 call sites, (c) making `--dry-run` actually skip the network on ~15 read commands, and (d) an unrelated CI harness test fix in `scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs`. Each is independently reviewable, testable and revertable; the CI-harness hunk in particular has nothing to do with CLI auth, URL encoding, or dry-run and belongs in its own change. No originating issue text accompanied this review, so I cannot cite a criterion — but the bundling itself makes it impossible to tell which of the four was requested.

The new user-facing `login --allow-unbound-callback` flag is not reflected in the CLI's two self-description surfaces. `registry.ts`'s `login` entry lists only `--server`, yet the registry is otherwise exhaustive per command (`--force`, `--yes`, `--out` all appear), and `docs/design/cli.md` §4's command tree line for `login` (line 311) lists no options while every other command spells its flags out in brackets. cli.md documents `wafflebase schema` as the runtime contract agents read, so a security-relevant opt-out flag that is absent from it (and described only in §3.1 prose) is an incomplete surface.
samples.evidence: registry.ts:43-50 `name: 'login'` with parameters `{'--server': ...}` only; cli.md:311 `├── login  Browser OAuth login → writes session`
searchedFor: grep "'--force'|'--yes'|'--out'" in registry.ts to confirm exhaustiveness

samples.summary: The stated invariant "the preview is the request" is only achieved for segment *encoding*, not for path *shape*. `cells get` re-implements HttpClient's three-way endpoint selection (range → `?range=`, bare ref → `/cells/<ref>`, none → `/cells`) and its range encoding inside the dry-run branch, and `sheets-export.ts:46-55` likewise re-derives `/documents/<id>/tabs/<tab>/cells?range=`. The new `url.ts` sharing stops at `seg()`; the URL shapes remain duplicated between the command layer and `http-client.ts`, so a route change can still leave the preview describing a request nobody sends — exactly the drift the change says it eliminated for `apiKeysUrl()`. Deriving the preview path from the client (as done for api-keys) would be the consistent shape.

The change adds a second per-flow secret (`cliState`) alongside the existing `csrf` field, which is generated and returned by `createState`/`consumeState` but is never read or validated anywhere in `packages/backend/src` (only its own spec references it). Meanwhile `docs/design/rest-api.md`'s risk table — a table this change edits and appends to — still claims "OAuth state forgery (CSRF) | Backend generates a random 32-byte CSRF token ... and validates on callback", and the CLI Auth Endpoints section reasserts that the CSRF token is "embedded in the encoded state". Either the dead `csrf` should have been the mechanism reused/removed, or the doc claim corrected while this section was being rewritten.
samples.evidence: grep -i csrf over packages/backend/src returns only cli-auth.store.ts, its spec, and an unrelated cookie comment in auth.controller.ts:262

samples.summary: The one-time `GET /start` redirect hop is scope beyond the callback-binding goal and adds new user-visible failure modes the design doc does not address: a browser link prefetch, an antivirus/URL scanner, or a user re-opening the printed URL (e.g. after the first tab was closed, or pasting it into a second browser) consumes the single use and gets `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, forcing a full re-run of `wafflebase login`. cli.md §3.1 documents the single-use property purely as a security benefit and never mentions that ordinary browser behaviour can burn it. The argv/stderr-leak hardening it buys is explicitly acknowledged in the same paragraph as incomplete (a racing local process still wins), so the cost/benefit of the extra route deserves an explicit note or a retry-tolerant design.

finding.summary: Single-use `/start` is at odds with the documented headless copy-paste path it is supposed to preserve
finding.evidence: cli.md:176-178 now says step 3 "Opens (and prints, for copy-paste in headless environments) the nonce-free http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start", and cli.md:206-211 claims "the URL a headless user copies is the same one `open()` is given and the same one that works". Those two properties cannot both hold with a one-shot route: `login` always calls `open(startUrl)` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:72) and only falls into the `catch` when the dynamic import or spawn itself throws — `open()` resolves normally in headless/CI environments where a launcher binary exists (xdg-open, `start`, wslview) but no browser ever renders, and browsers can also issue more than one request to a URL (prefetch/preconnect, restored tab). In those cases the first `GET /start` consumes the nonce and the URL the CLI just told the user to visit ("If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.", login.ts:68) answers `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, leaving the invocation with no way to complete — a regression against the prior behaviour, which printed a URL that still worked when the browser did not appear. The design doc asserts the property rather than reconciling it (e.g. allowing re-issue until the callback arrives, or only arming single-use after a successful open).

verdict.reason: The finding's stated mechanism is not how the code behaves. `startConsumed` is set only inside the `/start` request handler (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:266-281), so the nonce is consumed only by an actual `GET /start`. In the headless case the finding describes — `open()` resolving because a launcher binary exists while no browser ever renders — nothing requests `/start`, so the printed URL (login.ts:67-68, :399) still answers a 302 and the copy-paste fallback works precisely when it is needed. `login` itself never fetches `startUrl`; the only call is `await open(startUrl)` (login.ts:70-75). The two documented properties are therefore compatible in the case the fallback covers. The secondary claim that "the design doc asserts the property rather than reconciling it" is also contradicted by the doc: cli.md:191-192 says the route is served "(once)", cli.md:209-210 states the second `GET /start` is answered `410` in the same sentence as the property, and cli.md:216-223 names the accepted tradeoff ("single use means it steals the nonce only by breaking the login visibly") and the future PKCE-shaped endpoint that would close it. The remaining sliver (a browser issuing a duplicate request, or opening on an invisible display) would at most make the phrase "the same one that works" slightly over-broad — a doc-precision nit under the design-fit rubric, and a runtime-robustness question owned by the correctness lens. The required design doc exists, is the canonical docs/design/cli.md rather than a parallel file, and documents the shipped behavior, so no design-fit acceptance criterion, Non-Goal, or duplication rule is breached.
